answer: Reputation is issued, not claimed. Each identity holds a credential naming its sponsor and a bounded quota of sub-credentials; rewards vest across epochs to the credential, not the key. Anyone may prove two credentials share a spawn, and an upheld proof climbs the ancestry, revoking unvested balances beneath it. A farm faces two bad options: gather its heads under one ancestor, where one proof takes the whole vine, or buy N sponsors each risking standing on a stranger. Each added head widens what a challenger may strike and delays the nectar, so no voyage of copies repays its risk.
